subject: Regional routing & throughput/latency qualification — action items and clarification
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthlink.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@healthlink.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap — regional latency / throughput constraints

Evelyn / team,

Thanks for the demo earlier today — quick recap and a list of performance / residency asks so we can move to a qualification run: 

Top-level requirements from our product/infra leads:
- Per-user routing: EU users' requests must stay in EU region and any logs/eval data must not leave EU (GDPR + local certification).
- Latency targets (customer goals, negotiable): p95 end-to-end for short responses (~<64 tokens) at <=150ms; for longer generation/streaming responses first-byte <500ms and per-token steady-state latency as low as possible.
- Throughput/concurrency: expected steady-state 300 reqs/min (5 reqs/sec) with 50 concurrent active clients; burst to 200 concurrent for spikes.
- Streaming: ~30% of requests require chunked streaming with immediate first-byte (under 500ms) and keep-alive of open stream for up to 30s.
- Fallback: must be able to fall back to smaller model variant in case of regional capacity constraints.
- Data controls: customer-managed KMS for keying, audit logs for all model calls, and region-scoped KV cache (no cross-border cache replication).

Action items for Redwood: can you confirm region-scoped KV cache + VPC-only egress for EU, provide a recommended model/config (quantization/profile) to hit targets, and propose a perf run plan (duration, traffic shape, metrics collected)?

Attached: call-recording + a small sample of sample prompts we'll use.

Thanks,
Liam
Account Executive — HealthLink
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthlink.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — regional latency / throughput constraints

Liam — thanks for the clear list. Welcome, Priya.

Quick acknowledgements and clarifying Qs before we finalize the perf plan:
1) Data residency: we can do region-scoped KV cache and support VPC-only egress for the private deployment. For hosted we can pin EU-only processing with separate provisioned capacity — we'll confirm audit log residency detail. Is HealthLink planning to use Private (VPC) or Redwood Hosted for the initial pilot?
2) Traffic shape: please confirm the distribution (US:EU:APAC) and percent of requests that are streaming vs non-streaming. The sample CSV you mentioned would help.
3) Targets: p95 150ms for short responses is aggressive but feasible in US with the right model/instance class and batching config. We'll propose a 48-hour qualification run that includes a 6-hour burst window to validate concurrency and fallback.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- Rishi will draft a region-aware perf config and recommended model variants.
- We will provide perf_probe_instructions.md and a small test harness (link below) to run an initial smoke test with your dev team.
- Schedule a 30-minute sync with infra leads (can we do Friday 28 May 09:00 PT?)

I attached the probe instructions and the PSA for our pilot. If you can send the sample traffic CSV (format: timestamp,region,payload_tokens,is_streaming) we'll map it into the harness.

Evelyn
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
Evelyn Hart | Director, Strategic Accounts | redwood.ai
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthlink.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 02:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — regional latency / throughput constraints

Evelyn / Liam — quick technical write-up so we're aligned before the perf run: 

Summary of what we can commit to for the qualification run (not final SLA):
- Region-scoped processing: for Private deployments (VPC) we guarantee no egress from the chosen region if configured; for Hosted we offer EU-only capacity nodes for EU traffic and can ensure logs stay in-region for retention windows. We'll provide an architecture diagram in the run doc.
- KV cache: can be configured to be region-scoped. We will not replicate KV entries cross-region unless explicitly enabled.
- Model variants & suggested instance sizing: primary recommendation redwood-kestrel-2.3-16q on 1x A100-equivalent instance per 200 qps for low latency interactive workloads; fallback redwood-kestrel-1.9-8q or 1.7-8q for capacity shortage (lower mem / faster cold-starts). These model names are suggestions — we'll include benchmark numbers in the run report.
- Latency guidance: based on our benchmarks (no batching, single-turn short prompt ~32 tokens): US p95 token-latency ~90–130ms; EU p95 ~120–180ms (network egress + opaque infra); APAC p95 ~170–260ms depending on region. For streaming first-byte we expect ~150–350ms in US/EU with optimized routing.
- Concurrency & bursts: we can sustain 50 persistent concurrent streams per instance class with autoscaling to cover 200 concurrent within a 6–12 minute cold-start window (depends on model warm state).

What we need from HealthLink to run a representative test:
1) hl_sample_traffic.csv (timestamp,region,payload_tokens,is_streaming) — please include 10k lines representing a 24–48 hour window.
2) A list of the top 20 prompts and any prompt-engineering/templating you use.
3) If you're using customer-managed KMS, a contact for engineering to coordinate key rotation and provisioning (we integrate with AWS KMS & Cloud HSM).

Perf run plan (proposed):
- Smoke test (2 hours) — confirm connectivity and basic metrics
- Baseline (24 hours) — steady-state mix at expected throughput
- Burst validation (6 hours) — scripted spikes to 200 concurrent
- Streaming stability (12 hours) — keep-alive and first-byte metrics
- Post-run report: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, failures, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, end-to-end e2e traces for sample requests.

I'll prepare a run config and upload to the Drive link. Happy to jump on Fri 28 if that works for infra.

—Rishi
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthlink.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@healthlink.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 01:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — regional latency / throughput constraints

Evelyn / Rishi — this is great, thanks. Priya and I attached a 10k-line sample (hl_sample_traffic.csv) with regional flags and the top-20 prompts. A few clarifications:
- We intend to start on Hosted EU-only capacity for the pilot but will evaluate Private later this year.
- EU user base is primarily Germany/France/Netherlands; APAC customers are Singapore + Sydney.
- For compliance we need confirmation that any debug traces that contain PII can be redacted before leaving EU; we'd prefer those traces never leave region.
- Timeline: we are asking to start the baseline perf run week of 31 May and aim to make a procurement decision by mid-June.

Can you confirm you can begin smoke tests Tuesday 1 June? Also please send a short SOW/PSA that covers the qualification scope and responsibilities.

Thanks,
Liam

Attachments: hl_sample_traffic.csv, top_20_prompts.txt

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@healthlink.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap — regional latency / throughput constraints

Liam — excellent, thanks for the sample. Confirmed next steps and owners below so HealthLink has a clear cadence: 

Owners & timeline:
- Evelyn (go-to-customer): scheduling, commercial coordination, SOW/PSA, HubSpot updates (start this morning).
- Rishi (technical run lead): upload run config to the Drive and validate smoke test connectivity (target: 2027-06-01 for smoke).
- Monica (CS/ops): will coordinate KMS onboarding and collect the contact list for security questionnaires.
- Karthik (solutions): will validate prompt set and do an initial cold-run with the harness to sanity-check token distributions.

Deliverables we will share before the smoke test:
- perf_probe_instructions.md (attached) with curl examples and metrics endpoints.
- SOW/PSA draft for the qualification (attached redwood-inference-psa.pdf) and a short statement of work we will mail by EOD.
- Drive folder with run configuration & expected metric dashboards.

Meeting: I'm creating the Friday 28 09:00 PT sync. If the time doesn't work for HealthLink please propose an alternative (we can move to 10:30 PT).

Next asks for HealthLink:
- Confirm Hosted EU-only pilot is acceptable for initial run.
- Send contact for KMS and Security POA for redaction/trace handling.

I'll update the HubSpot deal (HL-2027-0953) and share the invite. Looking forward to the run — we'll capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, KV hit rates, and trace snippets per the plan.

Evelyn
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
